first_hunter_context.bar: Q3 2026 revenue ~$20.12-20.13B: Zacks $20.13B (https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3010051/), Fiscal AI $20.115B (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/axp-gets-a-slew-of-price-target-cuts-ahead-of-q3-report-this-month-latest-targets-still-show-room-for-upside/cZDpv06RBSw), Benzinga $20.12-20.13B. The sources agree. EPS sources are spread: $4.47 (Zacks, two downward revisions in 7 days), $4.54 (Fiscal AI), $4.58 (Earnings Whispers), $4.59-4.60 (Benzinga). All exclude the ~$1.10/share GBTG gain. The company guide is FY2026 revenue growth of 10% and EPS of $17.30-17.90, explicitly ex-gain (https://sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/4962/000000496226000318/q226exhibit991.htm). The revenue bar is consistent with the guide: H2 needs ~+9.3% and consensus Q3 is +9.2% on $18.43B.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest is about 11.5M shares, ~1.7% of ~675M shares outstanding, at 3.8 days to cover. This is the FINRA 2026-07-15 settlement via a curvedtrading.com search snippet (snippet_only; the page returned 403; https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/axp/short-interest/). It was 10.8M / 2.9 days at 2026-06-30. Not a crowded short. The baseline skew is +0.65 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 1.25, and front-expiry OI is thin (5,197). The event-implied move of 4.49% is rich against a 2.35% median historical reaction. The stock is -15.9% from its 52-week high and up +5.91% over 20 days. It traded near $303 pre-market on 2026-10-05 (stocktwits) and $323.71 at the seal, after Barclays, UBS and Evercore cut targets to $342/$345/$320.

evidence.text: AXP's own 8-K of 2026-10-15 shows Q3 2026 U.S. Consumer card net write-offs (principal only) at 1.6%, against 1.8% in Q2 2026. Q2 had been flattered ~0.3pp in June by a sale of written-off balances, so the underlying improvement is ~0.3pp. U.S. Small Business was 2.3% against 2.4%. Held-for-investment balances grew to $160.9B from $159.7B. 30+ day delinquency ticked up to 1.2% (Consumer) from 1.1%, and to 1.4% (Small Business) from 1.3/1.4%. Q3 2025 company-wide net write-offs were 1.9% and Q3 2025 provision was $1,287M (Q2 2026 deck). Lower write-offs point to a provision at or below Q2's $1,084M against a large y/y comparison, which supports EPS ex-items above the $4.47-4.60 consensus. The delinquency uptick limits any reserve release.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026, credit was strong (a $191M reserve release, write-offs flat at 2.0%) and EPS beat ($4.53 vs ~$4.41), yet the stock fell 4.3% on the print day (baseline 2026-07-24) because the EPS guide was held. Credit beats have not been paid for on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is public eight days before the print and sell-side models read it, so it is largely in consensus. Zacks nonetheless shows two downward EPS revisions in the last seven days, not upward ones. If the market had fully priced lower write-offs, revisions would be drifting up rather than down.
evidence.independence: JPMorgan Q3 2026 Card Services NCO fell to 2.91% from 3.15% y/y (https://www.pymnts.com/?p=4306652). Citi U.S. cards NCLs were down 4% y/y (https://www.panabee.com/news/citigroup-earnings-q3-2026). These are different issuers, so they point the same way independently.

evidence.text: Delta's September-quarter 2026 release (2026-10-09) is a direct counterparty that spoke after AXP last did. It reports American Express remuneration +15% y/y (Q2: +16%, $2.4B), co-brand card acquisitions and spend both growing double digits for the eighth straight quarter, and FY remuneration above $9B. Delta's corporate sales grew double digits in all sectors and its total revenue rose ~16% on yields. This supports AXP's T&E billed business (T&E is 28% of billed business, airlines 6%; Q2 T&E +10%) and card-fee growth, at about the Q2 pace with no acceleration.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Billed-business growth of 9% with a raised revenue guide in Q2 2026 still drew a -4.3% day. Billing strength on its own has not moved this stock up.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public and read by card analysts. The remuneration growth rate is steady, not accelerating (15% vs 16%), so it confirms the run-rate in consensus rather than exceeding it. Had the market treated it as upside, revenue estimates would sit above the $20.27B that a straight 10% y/y implies, and they sit at $20.13B.
evidence.independence: Delta's Q2 2026 release (https://s2.q4cdn.com/181345880/files/doc_earnings/2026/q2/earnings-result/Delta-Air-Lines-Announces-Second-Quarter-2026.pdf) gives the comparison. The industry spend finding below comes from different documents.

evidence.text: Q3 2026 card spending was strong at other issuers that reported after AXP's last print. JPMorgan debit and credit sales volume was +10% y/y to ~$539.5B. Citi general-purpose credit card spend was +13% y/y, flattered by the American Airlines portfolio onboarding. BofA Institute's September card spending per household was +6.2% y/y, the 'third strongest in four years', with breadth across income cohorts. Against AXP's own Q2 billed-business growth of +9% FX-adjusted, this is consistent with billed business holding ~9% or better and revenue at or slightly above the 9.2% y/y in consensus. It is a proxy only: AXP's affluent and commercial mix differs, and Commercial Services grew only 5% in Q2.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue was $19.64B against ~$19.70B consensus, a slight miss despite +9% billings, and the stock fell. Revenue lines have decided the reaction here more than EPS.
evidence.why_not_priced: These are wire-level macro prints, so the market has seen them. The transmission to AXP's own billings is unconfirmed. If it were fully priced, the revenue consensus would already have moved above the 10% FY guide pace, and it has not.
evidence.independence: BofA Institute Consumer Checkpoint, 2026-10-09 (https://institute.bankofamerica.com/economic-insights/consumer-checkpoint-october-2026.html). Citi Q3 2026 (https://vestedfinance.com/blog/us-stocks/citigroup-q3-earnings-2026/). These are separate documents from JPM's. The Delta finding is a separate counterparty.

evidence.text: The GBTG stake sale closed inside Q3: Long Lake completed the GBTG take-private on 2026-09-29. AXP had said it would book ~$975M pre-tax gain on ~$1.5B proceeds, 'not factored into the FY 2026 earnings guidance', and would 'invest a portion... and return a portion to shareholders'. At a ~24% tax rate that is ~$740M, or roughly +$1.10 on Q3 GAAP EPS against a $4.47-4.60 consensus that excludes it. The headline EPS will read as a large beat, and the FY GAAP guide may be lifted to include the gain. The market will look through it. It matters only through how much is redeployed into marketing and buybacks, and whether the ex-gain EPS guide moves.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No same-line history in the baseline. In Q2 2026 the 'reaffirm EPS guide with increased investments' framing drew -4.3%, so redeploying gains into spend has not been rewarded.
evidence.why_not_priced: The gain itself is public, and a below-the-line gain is seen through, so its price value is near zero. What is not priced is the use of the gain. If the market expected it to fund a buyback or a guide raise, the stock would not be trading 16% below its high with target cuts into the print.
evidence.independence: The closing date comes from GBTG's 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001820872/000114036126037931/ef20082602_ex99-1.htm) and AXP's Q2 10-Q ('sizable pre-tax gain... in Other expense', https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/4962/000000496226000322/axp-20260630.htm). It shares the 'invest a portion' language with the expense finding, which is sized net of this.

evidence.text: On 2026-10-08 AENB consented to an OCC cease-and-desist order with a $350M civil money penalty, plus a Fed order, over BSA/AML deficiencies (~$13B of suspected trade-based laundering went unreported). AXP says a portion was reserved in prior periods; the Q2 10-Q cites 'an increase in legal reserves'. There is no asset cap, and AXP says there is no impact on FY2026 or 2027 guidance. The unreserved remainder, which is non-deductible, will likely be booked as a Q3 charge because the order came before the books closed. Its size is undisclosed: it could be roughly $0.05-0.25 per share.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline. The news itself landed 2026-10-08, during the +6.8% rebound from early-October lows, so the market did not treat it as material.
evidence.why_not_priced: The headline is priced. The Q3 charge remainder is not quantified anywhere, and it may be part of why Zacks consensus drifted down to $4.47. It is a one-off with no stated path to the guide, so it is sized near zero.
evidence.independence: OCC release (https://occ.gov/news-issuances/news-releases/2026/nr-occ-2026-87.html). Banking Dive (https://www.bankingdive.com/news/amex-dinged-by-fed-occ-must-pay-350m-for-aml-failures/832570/): no reserved figure given.

evidence.text: Expense pressure, from AXP's Q2 2026 deck. Total expenses grew +12% against revenue +10%. Card Member Services was +50% ($1,949M vs $1,301M) on the U.S. Platinum refresh and benefit usage. Variable customer engagement costs were 44.6% of revenue (+17%). The EPS guide was held 'with increased investments in growth opportunities'. With the GBTG gain earmarked partly for investment, Q3 marketing and opex are likely to step up. That risks a weaker pre-tax margin ex-gain and a 'quality of beat' read even if revenue lands.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: EPS beat, expenses +12%, guide held, -4.3% on the day (baseline). The market has punished expense growth outrunning revenue growth.
evidence.why_not_priced: The run-rate is known. What is unknown is the size of Q3 redeployment funded by the gain. If the market expected spend to be contained, there would be no valuation-led target cuts (Evercore to $320, UBS to $345) into the print.
evidence.independence: This shares the GBTG 'invest a portion' release with the one-off finding; that finding is sized net of this redeployment. Q2 10-Q expense commentary: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/4962/000000496226000322/axp-20260630.htm

evidence.text: AXP guided at Q2 that net card fee growth (15% FX-adjusted in Q2) would accelerate in Q3 and exit Q4 in the high teens, helped by the Platinum refresh, now 'the fastest growing' U.S. Consumer portfolio. Public Platinum welcome offers in October 2026 run up to 175,000 MR points on the $895 card, with higher offers tested in August, which is consistent with an acquisition push. This lands inside what the company already guided.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Card fees grew 15-17% through 2025-26 while the stock fell after most prints. This line has not driven reactions.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is guided, so consensus carries it. Only a miss on the acceleration would surprise, and nothing found suggests one.
evidence.independence: Motley Fool October 2026 offer roundup (https://www.fool.com/money/credit-cards/articles/best-amex-cards-this-month-oct-2026/). This is a proxy for acquisition intensity, not fee revenue.

evidence.text: Positioning and reaction function. AXP fell after 6 of its last 7 prints (median |move| 2.35%; -4.3% on 2026-07-24 after an EPS beat with a raised revenue guide and a held EPS guide; -4.31% on 2026-04-23). It now enters the print up ~6.8% from its ~$303 early-October low to $323.71 (5-day +3.14%). In early October, Barclays ($342), UBS ($345) and Evercore ($320) cut targets on sector valuation (inflation, AI concerns), and the Koyfin split is 14 Hold vs 15 Buy. Short interest is not crowded (~1.7%), so there is no squeeze mechanism. A sell-the-news reaction to an ordinary beat is the base case for this name.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: 1 up in 7 (+7.27% on 2025-10-17, the only up print, which came with a guide raise). Every print without an EPS-guide raise has fallen.
evidence.why_not_priced: The options are balanced (skew +0.65) and the implied move of 4.49% is nearly double the median reaction, so the market prices size, not sign. The rebound into the print raises the bar for 'good enough'. If the market had priced a sell-the-news outcome, the stock would not have rallied ~7% in the last two and a half weeks.
evidence.independence: Sealed baseline reaction history (8-K 2.02 acceptance times). Q2 reaction coverage: https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/stock-market-news/company--news/american-express-lifts-revenue-outlook-after-strong-quarter,-but-shares-fall

evidence.text: OCC order requires an action plan within 90 days and a third-party SAR look-back; any further remediation cost or business restriction surfaces after the window.
Visa and Mastercard September-quarter prints (cross-border and U.S. payments volume read-through) are scheduled after 2026-10-23, so the market cannot see them inside the window.

YTD consolidated net income is $25.0M, and remaining land sales are expected in Q4. first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest is 372.2K shares with 3.5 days to cover at the FINRA settlement of 2026-07-15 (snippet via search; https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/fph/short-interest/ returned 403). Days to cover were 2.3 at 2026-06-30. Against about 71.8M Class A shares (10-Q, 2026-07-17 count), that is roughly 0.5% of float, not crowded. No usable option chain: total OI 27, ATM not two-sided, no skew. Tape: spot 4.565, -27.5% from the 52-week high and +7.4% above the low, 20-day -3.3%, 5-day +6.7%. The stock was $5.16 on 2026-08-24, so a macro selloff has already taken place into the print.

evidence.text: The 2026 guide of about $100M consolidated net income needs about $75-80M in Q4 alone: $25.0M YTD through June, and Q3 is guided as a no-land-sale quarter. Land-sale timing has already slipped once. On 2026-04-23 management said transactions would close 'in the third and fourth quarters'. On 2026-07-23 it said 'our remaining land sales activity will occur in the fourth quarter' and declined to update the guide, citing interest rates and affordability. With one quarter left, this call must reaffirm with named contracts (five Great Park residential programs, about 28.5 acres, plus Valencia homesites 'in documentation') or move some closings into 2027.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide has driven this name's largest moves. Jan 2026, when the 2026 guide of about $100M (against $176M in 2025) was set: -5.01%. Jul 2025: -14.93%. Jan 2025: +41.63%. The two reaffirmations, Apr 2026 (+0.99%) and Jul 2026 (+4.39%, with a land sale), moved little.
evidence.why_not_priced: The guide was reaffirmed twice and no analyst publishes a revision. If the market fully priced a slip, consensus or a note would show a 2026 net income well under $100M, and none is visible. Pricing a full slip would also take more than the roughly 17% drop since late August, which coincides with the rate move rather than with any company news.
evidence.independence: Same company, earlier document: Q1 2026 release (2026-04-23) placed closings in Q3 and Q4, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260423513937/en/Five-Point-Holdings-LLC-Reports-First-Quarter-2026-Results. Q2 call: closings moved to Q4 and 'market conditions could alter the timing', https://www.webull.com/news/15278768186156032.

evidence.text: Since the company last spoke on 2026-07-23, when the 30-year mortgage rate was about 6.7% (Freddie Mac, 6.69% on 2026-08-06), the rate has risen to 7.28% on 2026-10-01 (highest since Nov 2023) and 7.40% on 2026-10-15. The 10-year Treasury was reported at its highest level since 2007 in late September. Management named rates and affordability as the things that could move Q4 land-sale timing.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No company-specific history. The share price fell from $5.16 (2026-08-24) to about $4.28 a week before the print while rates rose, so the stock has traded this series already.
evidence.why_not_priced: The rate is public and the selloff partly prices it. What is not priced is whether a specific builder has paused or retraded a Q4 Great Park or Valencia closing, which only the call reveals. A market that had priced a slip would show a lower 2026 number somewhere, and none exists.
evidence.independence: Proxy: macro-to-company transmission that the company has not confirmed. The 7.40% figure on 2026-10-15 is from a secondary site (https://mortgage-info.com/blog/10-year-treasury-yield-mortgage-rates-october-2026), not a Freddie Mac primary release. This finding shares its mechanism with the builder-counterparty finding, so both are sized small.

evidence.text: Builder counterparties spoke after FPH did and both said conditions worsened. Lennar, a Great Park buyer (property records show about $121.5M of a $218M Great Park parcel), cut its 2026 delivery target to 80-81K from 82-83K on 2026-09-16, citing 'the deterioration in market conditions through the quarter', with orders down 9%. KB Home (2026-09-22) reported net orders down 12% and said conditions weakened since June. FPH's own Q2 numbers already showed builder home sales slowing: Great Park 56 against 82 in Q1, Valencia 78 against 90. The Q3 builder-sales figures will be in this release.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. Builder absorption is reported every quarter. The Q2 slowdown came alongside a +4.39% reaction, because a land sale outweighed it.
evidence.why_not_priced: Homebuilder results are public, but no FPH-specific estimate was revised on them, because the only covering analyst is silent. If the market had priced the read-through, the 2026 bar would sit below the guide, and nothing shows that.
evidence.independence: KB Home Q3 2026 (2026-09-22): orders -12%, conditions weakened, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000795266/000079526626000068/exh991kbh-earningsrelease0.htm. Lennar as a Great Park buyer: https://www.ocbj.com/real-estate/218m-land-deal-irvine/ (that article is undated). Shares its mechanism with the rate finding.

evidence.text: Toll Brothers, the luxury builder that bought 82 Great Park homesites for $74.6M, reported on 2026-08-18 fiscal Q3 net signed contract value of $2.52B, up from $2.41B, and 2,508 contracted homes against 2,388, with luxury demand holding up. Great Park is a high-price Irvine community, the segment that has held best.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated.
evidence.why_not_priced: The read-through to Great Park's high-end land demand is not in any FPH estimate. The proxy offsets part of the Lennar/KB read-through rather than adding new information.
evidence.independence: The Toll homesite purchase at Great Park was referenced in a search summary of FPH releases; the date of that purchase is not verified. Toll's results release is the source of the order numbers. Proxy.

evidence.text: On 2026-09-25 (8-K filed 2026-09-30), FPH renewed its Great Park Development Management Agreement, due to expire 2026-12-31, through 2028-12-31 on the same terms: $13.5M annual base fee and 9% incentive compensation on Great Park Venture distributions. After 2028, a tail of 6.75% of later distributions continues if the agreement is not extended. This removes an expiry risk on the largest fee stream; the Great Park fee was $9.1M of Q2's $14.7M management services revenue.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The previous renewal (third amendment, Sept 2024) was disclosed between prints. No isolated reaction is measured.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 8-K is public. On a one-analyst name, a renewal that extends recurring fee visibility two years may only be priced once management frames it on the call. Mostly priced, so sized small.
evidence.independence: Prior terms ($13.5M base fee, 9% incentive) are confirmed in the 2024 renewal coverage: https://bulletin.webull.com/20240918/171186/bcb2bdc8f835cc79aad3afa47777531b.html

evidence.text: The board approved a $40M share repurchase authorization in April 2026. In Q2, FPH bought 623,432 Class A shares for $3.1M at about $4.96. The stock traded lower through Q3 (about $4.3-5.2) and cash was $348.4M at June 30, so Q3 likely shows larger repurchases, which management frames against the discount to book.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 print that announced the authorization moved +0.99%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Q3 repurchase amount is not public until the 10-Q or release. An acceleration at sub-$5 prices would be the company acting on the discount, and no one has quantified it. The amount is inferred, not known.
evidence.independence: Q2 repurchase of 623,432 shares for $3.1M is in the 10-Q filed 2026-07-24: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1574197/000157419726000027/fph-20260630.htm

evidence.text: Q3 2026 itself should report no land sales: management placed all remaining 2026 closings in Q4. Consolidated results should look like Q1 2026 (-$5.0M net loss on $13.6M revenue, essentially management fees), against Q3 2025 consolidated net income of $55.7M, when the Great Park Venture sold 326 homesites for $257.7M. The year-on-year collapse is guided and inside the guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026, a quiet quarter with a -$5.0M net loss and no land sales, moved +0.99%. Quiet quarters have not been sold on the number.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is largely priced, because the company told the market. The residual is a headline year-on-year drop that an automated reader could misread.
evidence.independence: Q3 2025 comparison: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1574197/000157419725000082/ex-991xfphx93025x8k.htm

first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest on the INFY ADS 108.98M shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 7.39 days to cover, down from 125.12M (2026-09-15) and 129.80M (2026-08-31) (https://equibles.com/stocks/infy/shortinterest, read 2026-10-22); the 10-15 figure is not yet published. Much of this is likely ADR/local arbitrage rather than outright bearish. Skew: 25d put minus call +5.08 vol points, put/call OI 1.21, so downside is paid. Tape: run_up_20d +24.0%, run_up_5d +7.34%, still 35.6% below the 52-week high. Event-implied move 7.22%.

evidence.text: The FY27 guidance bar has been lowered: the company guide is +1.5-3.0% CC (narrowed from 1.5-3.5% on 2026-07-23), and the 2026-10-22 brokerage previews expect a trim to 1.5-2.5% (Emkay; JM Financial 2026-09-28 the same) or a narrowing to 2-3% (HDFC). Meanwhile the Q2 consensus of +1.1-1.7% QoQ CC sits at or above the 0.5-1.4% CQGR ask rate the current guide implies (PL, July). So holding the range or narrowing it upward would beat the expected trim, and a trim to 2.5% at the top is roughly what the Street already holds.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The ADR traded on the guide each time. 2026-01-14: guide raised to 3-3.5%, ADR +10.45% (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/infosys-infy-soars-10-45-100957350.html). 2026-04-24: first FY27 guide 1.5-3.5% read as cautious, NSE down as much as 4.87% intraday. 2026-07-23: top end cut to 3.0%, ADR -4.92% at 09:44 ET (https://www.rttnews.com/3670054/infosys-q1-net-profit-rises-revises-fy27-revenue-outlook-stock-down.aspx). October 2025: guide raised to 2-3%, NSE still -2%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The previews converge on a trim, so a held or upward-narrowed range is not the consensus case. If the market had priced a hold, the put skew would not be +5 and the previews would not lead with 'guidance cut'. The 24% run-up does show some of the relief is already in.
evidence.independence: Ask-rate arithmetic from a separate source, PL India 2026-07-24 (https://plindia.com/ResReport/INFO-24-7-26-PL.pdf), and the JM Financial expectation (https://businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/tcs-infosys-hcl-tech-techm-wipro-ltm-check-fresh-targets-for-top-it-stocks-ahead-of-q2-results-558244-2026-09-28). This is an inference on the guide and not a company document, so it is sized small.

evidence.text: This reporting season's reaction function has bought Indian IT prints: TCS +5.46% on 2026-10-09 (0.5% QoQ CC, in line, TCV $9.6bn), HCLTech +4-5% on 2026-10-13 (FY27 guide raised to 2.5-4%), Wipro NSE +6.5% on 2026-10-16 despite a Q3 guide of -1.5% to +0.5% and large-deal bookings -58.6%, and Tech Mahindra +7-8% on 2026-10-16. The exception was Persistent, -6% on mixed numbers.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peer pattern, not INFY's own. INFY's own guide-day reactions this year were -5% (twice) and +10.45%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: INFY's +24% 20-day and +7.3% 5-day run-up is the market already extrapolating the peer relief. What is left is the chance that the pattern of relief rallies on in-line prints carries to the last tier-1 name. Note that Wipro's ADR fell about 3% on its guide while the NSE line rose, so the ADR does not always follow.
evidence.independence: Wipro: https://upstox.com/news/market-news/stocks/wipro-shares-gain-6-5-despite-a-nearly-5-qo-q-fall-in-q2-earnings-sluggish-trends-ahead/article-201988/ ; TechM: https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/tech-mahindra-shares-surge-as-q2-margins-beat-estimates-check-brokerage-targets-561969-2026-10-16 ; HCLTech: https://upstox.com/news/market-news/earnings/news-2-0-159/article-201706/. All are peer proxies.

evidence.text: The relief is already in the price. The ADR is +24.0% over 20 days and +7.34% over 5 days into the print. The NSE line at Rs 1,156 on 2026-10-22 is within 3% of the Rs 1,186 consensus 12-month target, which Business Today itself calls limited upside. ADR short interest has already fallen from 129.8M (08-31) to 109.0M shares (09-30), so part of the covering fuel is spent, and the 25d put-call skew is +5.08 vol points.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-23: the ADR fell 2.06% overnight into the print and then another 4.92% on the guide trim. 2025-10: NSE fell for a fifth day after a beat with a raised guide (-2%). The name has sold good-enough prints when it went in strong.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is what IS priced. It is filed as the counterweight that a stranger reading only the peer and guidance findings would miss. If the run-up had not happened, the stock would sit near its July $10.4 level with a much lower bar for relief.
evidence.independence: Short-interest series from a separate source: https://equibles.com/stocks/infy/shortinterest. Skew and run-up from the sealed baseline.

evidence.text: Counterparty demand read-through is positive. Accenture (2026-10-01) guided FY27 at +3-6% local currency, above Street, with Q4 bookings of $22.2bn. HCLTech (2026-10-12) raised its FY27 CC guide to 2.5-4% from 1-4% with $3.26bn of new bookings. Both spoke after Infosys last did, on 2026-07-23.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: INFY ADR moved on peer reads before: +40% intraday spike on 2025-12-19 around the Accenture print (per the Infosys statement reported by letsdatascience). Its own guide-day moves are in finding 1.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, since both were public weeks ago and INFY rallied through them. What remains is whether management echoes it in the guide, which the trim-expecting previews do not assume.
evidence.independence: HCLTech investor release: https://www.hcltech.com/sites/default/files/document/open/quarter-results/2026-10/hcltech-Q2-fy27-Investor-release.pdf (a separate document).

evidence.text: Counterparty demand read-through is negative. Wipro's 2026-10-15 Q3 guide is -1.5% to +0.5% QoQ CC, IT services were flat QoQ in Q2, and large-deal bookings fell 58.6% to $674M. Wipro's ADR fell about 3% on the guide. This points to H2 furlough and discretionary softness, the line JM says Infosys's H2 commentary will be judged on.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: INFY's July trim was attributed to a soft macro environment and program terminations, and the ADR fell 4.9%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the NSE line of Wipro rallied anyway and INFY kept rising after it. It matters only if Infosys's H2 commentary echoes it.
evidence.independence: Wipro guide and bookings detail: https://ticker.finology.in/discover/market-update/wipro-q2-fy27-results-analysis. The same company, so this is one finding.

evidence.text: On 2026-10-08 the US Department of Labor suspended new and pending PERM (green-card labor certification) applications for eight firms including Infosys, citing alleged visa-programme misuse. Infosys filed a 6-K company statement dated 2026-10-10 (filed 2026-10-13) saying it does not anticipate a material impact. Its safe-harbor language now names 'pending litigation and the US government investigation' (the DOJ H-1B classification probe disclosed in October 2025).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on immigration. TCS (reporting the same day as the suspension), HCLTech and Wipro all rallied on their prints after it, and the INFY ADR rose about 5.3% on 2026-10-13.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced, because peers traded through it. The residual is call-time commentary on US delivery cost, local hiring or onsite mix in the H2 outlook, which no preview models.
evidence.independence: https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2026/10/11/india039s-infosys-does-not-expect-material-impact-from-us-perm-suspension ; https://wolfsdorf.com/dol-announces-perm-suspensions-for-microsoft-adobe-and-major-it-firms/

evidence.text: On the Q2 2026 call (2026-07-23), CEO Berman said JAKKS was on track for 'achieving potentially exceeding our initial plans' for 2026. POS at the top 2 US accounts was positive in H1 (double-digit in Q2), and new product was 'shipping now for fall planogram sets', i.e. into Q3. There is still no numeric guide, so this is tone against a 1-2 analyst EPS bar of $2.02-2.31 (vs $1.80 a year ago).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (revenue +7% vs consensus, tone 'developing as planned'): +2.90%. Q1 2026: +10.57%. Q4 2025: +23.73%. Q3 2025 (EPS $1.80 vs $2.12, revenue -34%): -5.13%. This name has bought beats on the last three prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: The words are three months old. They are probably partly in the 18% run-up, but the single estimate was cut ($2.37 to $2.31) after the call rather than raised. If the market fully believed 'exceeding plan', estimates would have gone up, not down.
evidence.independence: Same call as the front-weighting finding below (one document, two different facts). Q2 press release: 'good momentum heading into the second half' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1009829/000118518526003108/jakkex10-1.htm).

evidence.text: CFO Kimble on the same call: 2026 is planned 'a bit more front-weighted than normal given the strength of Super Mario', with 'no new toy introductions in the second half supporting holiday theatrical releases'. So Q3 growth should run below Q2's +17%. Consensus implies about +9% revenue and +12-28% EPS.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025, the last time the seasonal quarter disappointed (no theatrical tie-ins, revenue -34%, EPS miss): -5.13%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The run-up and an EPS bar 12-28% above last year suggest the market is extrapolating H1 strength. If this phasing were priced, the stock would not be at a 52-week high above most $28.50-30 targets.
evidence.independence: Same document as the finding above. Quartr summary repeats it (https://quartr.com/events/jakks-pacific-inc-jakk-q2-2026_ozuFuLen).

evidence.text: The Q3 2025 comp is very easy: net sales $211.2M (-34%), Toys/CP $156.1M (-40.9%), US -39.5%, driven by tariff-related cuts to direct-import orders. In 2026 the IEEPA tariffs were struck down and refunded (JAKKS booked $6.8M in Q2), and H1 shipments were over 75% FOB, 'the highest this decade'. The same recovery gave Q2 2026 +17% revenue and a 7% revenue beat. Consensus of about $230M is only +9%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026, the same recovery dynamic (revenue $139.2M vs $129.6M consensus): +2.90%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The comp is public, so it is partly priced. The revenue consensus (+9%) sits well below Q2's +17% on the same recovery. If the full recovery were priced, the revenue bar would sit closer to Q2's growth rate. Front-weighting (above) is the counter-reason, so this is sized small.
evidence.independence: Q2 2026 release with US +24.4% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1009829/000118518526003108/jakkex10-1.htm). Earnings Whispers Q2 revenue beat (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/JAKK). Toy Association on the IEEPA ruling and refunds (https://www.toyassociation.org/PressRoom2/News/2026-News/scotus-strikes-down-ieepa-tariffs-president-trump-issues-new-tariff-proclamation.aspx).

evidence.text: Peer and counterparty data since JAKKS last spoke: Hasbro Q3 2026 (2026-10-20) had Consumer Products revenue +4% and North America $504.9M (+5%), and raised full-year revenue growth to 7-9% cc. Target Q2 2026 (2026-08-19) had double-digit growth in Fun101 (incl. toys). Circana US toys H1 2026 were +17% in dollars, the best in six years.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history. JAKK rose +2.9% on 2026-10-20 (Hasbro day, 28.37 to 29.20), so the read-through has already traded.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: JAKK took +2.9% on the Hasbro day. What remains is that a single-analyst bar may not have been updated for it. Proxy only.
evidence.independence: Target 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000027419/000002741926000034/a2026q2ex-99.htm). Circana via Retail Dive 2026-08-20 (https://www.retaildive.com/news/us-toy-industry-best-first-half-performance-six-years/828162/). evidence.text: Disguise (JAKKS costumes, $55.1M in Q3 2025, -3.8%, about 26% of Q3 sales) has the KPop Demon Hunters costume licence for Halloween 2026, alongside Toy Story 5 and Sonic. Netflix says KPop Demon Hunters was 2025's most in-demand Halloween costume. Spirit Halloween lists it as a top 2026 trend, and Costumes were already +8% in Q2.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No separate costume-surprise history. Costumes are about a quarter of Q3 revenue, so the rest (toys, -41% last Q3) has to at least hold flat for this to show in the total.
evidence.why_not_priced: The licence is public, but the sell-in size is not. No sell-out or volume data exists in the public record, so this is a proxy sized small and net of the rest of the company.
evidence.independence: Netflix Tudum (https://www.netflix.com/tudum/articles/kpop-demon-hunters-disguise-costumes). evidence.text: AI Receptionist (AIR) paying customers have grown about 40% a quarter: 8,300 at end Q4-25, 11,800 at Q1-26 and 16,400 at Q2-26 (+400% YoY). Customers on a paid AI product are about 13% of ARR, double a year ago, and AI-led product ARR grew nearly 60% in H1. If that cadence held in Q3 (roughly 22-23k AIR customers), the run-rate supports another FY raise beyond the July guide (FY revenue $2.635-2.646B), and that raise is the line this stock has paid for.

evidence.text: Price far ahead of the published bar: spot $81.92 is at the 52-week high, +8.9% in five sessions into the print, about +187% YTD, and about 30% above the $57.64 mean target (6 Buy / 9 Hold). EPS consensus ($1.27-1.28) sits at the guide midpoint and has not been revised in 60 days. A beat-and-raise that only matches published estimates, like Q1's (+0.5%), or a Q3 narrowing of the FY range that trims the top (as in Nov 2025, -8.25%), risks a 'sell the news' on an extended name.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1-26 (2026-05-07) beat with a modest FY raise moved +0.5%. Q3-25 (2025-11-03) beat with a lowered FY revenue midpoint moved -8.25% (Seeking Alpha https://seekingalpha.com/news/4514199-ringcentral-slides-after-lowering-midpoint-of-full-year-2025-revenue-guidance).
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the mild put skew (+3.52 vol pts) already leans this way, which is why it is sized small. What may not be priced is that the 5-day +9% run-up has lifted the implicit whisper well above a published consensus that has not moved. Fully priced would look like steep put skew and a post-run-up pullback, and neither is in the baseline.
evidence.independence: MarketScreener 2026-10-21: +10.2% over 5 days and +186.9% YTD at $82.82 https://ca.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/RINGCENTRAL-INC-14383012/news/Ringcentral-Inc-Announces-General-Availability-of-Ai-Receptionist-50378577/ .
